statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-41246 (GHSA-x4mj-7f9g-29h4, GO-2026-5738): in Contour, the Kubernetes ingress controller for Envoy, values from an HTTPProxy's cookie path rewrite policies (spec.routes[].cookieRewritePolicies[].pathRewrite.value and spec.routes[].services[].cookieRewritePolicies[].pathRewrite.value) were inserted into the Lua code that Contour generates for Envoy's Lua HTTP filter without sufficient sanitization, so a user allowed to create or modify HTTPProxy resources could run code in Envoy. It is fixed in Contour 1.31.6, 1.32.5 and 1.33.4: https://github.com/projectcontour/contour/security/advisories/GHSA-x4mj-7f9g-29h4, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5738, https://github.com/projectcontour/contour/releases/tag/v1.33.4 . The Go vulnerability database lists no vulnerable functions for this entry. In 1.33.4 the fix is commits 72793e0, 2d1c174 and 3b70727 on release-1.33, which stop putting user-supplied values into the generated Lua code: https://github.com/projectcontour/contour/commit/3b70727f2aa622401f3b3d53b4401599d225b789 . Between v1.33.3 and v1.33.4, outside tests, examples, a CI workflow and the default Contour and Envoy image tags in cmd/contour/gatewayprovisioner.go, the only changed files are internal/dag/dag.go, internal/dag/policy.go, internal/envoy/v3/listener.go, internal/envoy/v3/route.go and internal/xdscache/v3/listener.go; the Lua code is built by cookieRewriteConfig in internal/envoy/v3, from the policies converted by cookieRewritePolicies in internal/dag. Nothing under apis/ changed. We downloaded every external-dns-dev package listed in the Alpine 3.23 index of the DHI Alpine repository, for x86_64 and aarch64: 33 versions from 0.20.0-r0 to the current 0.24.0-r5, each published for both architectures, and checked each download against the index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/external-dns, a Go program built with GOOS=linux and CGO_ENABLED=0, plus directories; no package contains a symbolic link. We read the function table (pclntab) and build information of the program in every build and searched its bytes, which also finds the names of inlined functions; runtime.main is in the function table of every build. The Go release by build: 0.20.0-r0 Go 1.25.7; 0.20.0-r1 to 0.21.0-r0 Go 1.26.1; 0.21.0-r1 to 0.21.0-r2 Go 1.26.2; 0.21.0-r3 to 0.21.0-r5 Go 1.26.3; 0.21.0-r6 to 0.21.0-r7 Go 1.26.4; 0.21.0-r8 to 0.21.0-r11 Go 1.26.5; 0.21.0-r12 Go 1.26.6; 0.21.0-r13 to 0.22.0-r0 Go 1.26.7; 0.22.0-r1 to 0.22.0-r3 Go 1.26.8; 0.23.0-r1 to 0.23.0-r2 Go 1.27.1; 0.23.0-r3 Go 1.27.2; 0.23.0-r4 to 0.24.0-r2 Go 1.27.3; 0.24.0-r3 to 0.24.0-r5 Go 1.27.4. The build information lists github.com/projectcontour/contour v1.33.0 in 0.20.0-r0 to 0.20.0-r4, v1.33.3 in 0.21.0-r0 to 0.21.0-r3, v1.33.4 in 0.21.0-r4 to 0.21.0-r8, v1.33.5 in 0.21.0-r9 to 0.21.0-r13, v1.33.6 in 0.22.0-r0 to 0.22.0-r3 and v1.33.7 in 0.23.0-r1 to 0.24.0-r5. In every build, every Contour function in the function table is in package github.com/projectcontour/contour/apis/projectcontour/v1, the HTTPProxy API types; no function from any github.com/projectcontour/contour/internal/ package is present. The byte search of every build finds neither github.com/projectcontour/contour/internal/ nor cookieRewriteConfig, and its one occurrence of cookieRewritePolicies is the JSON field tag of the HTTPProxy API type. As a positive control, the same function-table reader and byte search run on Contour's own contour program, built from v1.33.3 for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, find internal/envoy/v3.cookieRewriteConfig and internal/dag.cookieRewritePolicies in its function table and github.com/projectcontour/contour/internal/ in its bytes. The builds that list Contour 1.33.0 or 1.33.3 are inside the advisory's version range, but the vulnerable code is not compiled into any build of this package.
